reviewMethod: Official May 2026 TZ1-TZ3 questions: a source-grounded primary pass from the question crop and official markscheme, a separate blind second pass from sealed evidence without the primary labels or the Drex triage scores, and a written adjudication of every row where the passes differ (primary subtopic, primary code, code set or secondaries). Drex (drex-v2.0, text only) was used for triage only.

ownerReviewFixes.source: PR #305 owner review (2026-10-15), applied by the source lane after adjudication

adjudication.rationale: Answer needs U=3/2NkT to compare particle numbers (gas law) and then direction of heat flow from the temperature difference (B.1). Single mark, gas content dominant.
1-mark MCQ (D): fusion releases energy so the product has greater binding energy / mass defect; a single concept, no separate cluster for N3.
Single 1-mark item: energy density = E/V (key B), the fuel energy-source quantity. Fits energy sources (T4) better than mechanical work/power.

Marks: linearise 1/P vs V (a, 2), units of slope (b, 2), read graph (c, 1), intercept as systematic error (d, 2) are graph/data skills; gas-law context is the setting. Units earn a separate F1 cluster.
Refraction, wavelength change and TIR in (a) earn 7 marks, tied with forces in (b),(c)(ii) (7 marks, plus 1 for P=Fv); conduction in (d) earns 5. Tie broken to the first printed block, waves.

Marks: d(i)-(ii) angular momentum and rotational KE 5 (plus d(iii) rotational KE/thermal 2), a and c stellar 6, b(ii)-(iv) Coulomb potential 5, b(i) binding energy 2. Rotational mechanics is the largest single physics strand, stellar recall is spread over several parts.
Key A: centripetal force supplied by gravity F proportional to m/r^2 gives 1/8; Newtonian gravitation is the whole mark.
1-mark MCQ (D): force between parallel currents on each wire (field of one wire, force on the other, third-law equality), so D.2 with D.3.
MS key C: U proportional to N T gives more particles in X, then heat flows from hotter Y to X. One mark, ideal-gas internal energy dominant with thermal-contact direction.
Mechanics earns 8 marks (b buoyancy/acceleration/terminal speed 6, c friction and P=Fv 2) vs refraction/TIR 7 (a) and conduction 5 (d). Mechanics edges the waves cluster.

Key B: peak colour of a 6500 K star (Wien law, one idea) and redshift from recession (Doppler, second idea), roughly equal in one mark; stellar spectrum setting keeps R3 primary. B.1 in the primary pass is wrong, Wien law is B.2.
Insulated compression: Q=0 so W=500x0.10=50 J raises internal energy, about 4 K, key C. First-law reasoning for 1 mark.
Force qE on negative charge towards positive plate opposes weight, resultant qE-mg (key B); one 1-mark item, no separate cluster.
1-mark MCQ (C): photon wavelength from the n=4 to n=2 level difference via hc/dE, which is atomic energy-level physics (E.1) with no separate E.2 cluster.
Friction supplies centripetal force: mu m g = m v^2/R gives v=sqrt(mu g R), key D. Single mark, circular motion.
Marks split evenly: graph curve/linearise/plot point (c,d,e iii), uncertainty (e ii + error bar) and experimental control (a, b ii, 3 each). Drag physics is context; v=d/t is A.1.

Experimental design, conditions and systematic-error cause in (a),(b),(c)(ii) earn 5 of 9 marks, so F5 is dominant; graph gradient to get speed in (c)(i),(d) earns 4 (F4). Speed of sound measured is wave model C.2.

a, b(i), b(ii) earn 4 marks from GPE, KE and work against friction; c-d earn 4 marks from rolling energy with I=2/5MR^2 and ring comparison. Tie broken toward energy since c also uses energy conservation.
Kinetic-model pressure (b, 2) and DeltaU=3/2nRDeltaT (c, 3) are gas-law marks; adiabatic TV^(2/3)=const (d, 2) is the thermodynamics cluster; a (1) is P=VIt only.
Snell's law (a, 2), critical angle (b, 1) and refraction/TIR path (c, 3) are all wave refraction, which fits W2 (wave model) better than interference/diffraction W3; all six marks are C.3.
c and d (3 marks) use qvB=mv^2/R and radii of isotopes; a (2) is qV=1/2mv^2, e (2) is grating n lambda=d sin theta, b (1) is a brief relativity check not worth a secondary.
Beta-minus, neutrino spectrum and decay-law dating (a-c, 6 marks) are radioactivity; binding energy per nucleon curve and mass-defect calc (d, 3) form a separate binding-energy cluster.

Kinematics e(ii) v^2=2gh (2) plus a-t area f(i),(ii) (3) = 5 marks, tied with forces c (3) and terminal-speed g (2); thermal d 3, gas law b 2, field e(i) 2. Tie broken to kinematics, a graph-and-motion theme.
Force qE on the negative charge is upward and opposes weight, resultant qE-mg (key B). One-mark electric-field force question.
Photon wavelength from n=4 to n=2 energy levels via hc/DeltaE (key C); discrete energy levels is the whole mark.
Same question as the HL version (key B): Wien-law peak colour of a star plus Doppler redshift in one mark; labelled consistently with HL.

Marks split a, b(ii) design 3; c, d graph 2; e(i)-(iii) speed, percentage uncertainty (2) and error bar 5 in total; part (e) is the largest coherent cluster and is uncertainty handling. Terminal-speed physics is context only (b(i) 1 mark).
Experimental design and evaluation (a 2, b 1, c(ii) 2) earn 5 of 9 marks; systematic error evidence (c i) is F2 and gradient for speed (d, 3) is F4. Speed of sound is wave-model context.
(b) kinetic-model explanation of pressure at constant volume (2 marks) dominates; (a) E=VIt (1 mark) is just the heater-energy setup, too small to be a secondary cluster.
Snell's law with wave speeds (a, 2), critical angle (b, 1) and refraction/TIR path (c, 3) all earn marks from refraction of waves at boundaries.
Isotopes from differing masses (b, 1) and photon energy difference of spectral lines (c, 2) give 3 atomic marks vs 2 for proton circular motion R=mv/qB (a). Part (a) is the separate E3 cluster.
Decay type, nucleon conservation and half-life for dating (a, b: 3 marks) tie with binding energy per nucleon from mass defect (c: 3 marks); all of it is E.3 content, so no N5 secondary is needed.

Multi-topic 20-marker: forces c buoyancy/N2 (3) plus g terminal speed (2) =5 ties with kinematics e(ii) and f (5); also d thermal 3, b gas law 2, e(i) g 2, h infrared 2. Forces and kinematics tie, M2 chosen for the 3-mark buoyancy/Newton calculation.
Work per unit charge between X and Y with sign of charge (key C); potential difference concept, circuit is only context.
1-mark MCQ (A): independence of vertical fall time from horizontal motion and range comparison; kinematics, drag is only the context.
Galaxy receding gives Doppler redshift, key B (lines shifted towards red). Pure Doppler idea for 1 mark.
Motional emf: free electron has balancing electric and magnetic forces (key A); one item, no separate cluster.
1-mark MCQ (C): photon energies from level differences compared with visible and UV ranges; energy-level transitions, E.1.
Beta-plus decay p -> n + e+ + neutrino (key B); radioactive decay process, 1 mark.
Rate of GPE change equals power 2Fv cos(theta) (key D); work/power is the assessed idea.
Marks are for reading the F-x line (a, 2), gradient (b, 2), equating gradient to rho*A*g and using the intercept (c, d, 5); the buoyancy relation is given, so graph modelling dominates.
a (2, specific/latent heat) and b(i) (3, internal energy as random KE plus PE) are thermal concepts = 5 marks; entropy dS=Q/T and second law b(ii)-(iii) are 3 marks.
Field E=V/d, F=qE, acceleration and alpha comparison (a i-ii, b i) earn 6 of 11; a(iii) 3-mark projectile kinematics check is M1; b(ii) qvB=qE balance (2) is E3.
Interference in (c)(iii),(iv),(d) earns 7 marks, the largest single subtopic; mechanics is split across Hooke/equilibrium M2 (3), elastic energy M3 (4) and impulse M4 (3), and SHM (c)(i) 2.
a(i)-(iii) and b(i) escape speed, energy conservation, field strength earn 8 marks; stellar R4 about 7 (c, d(ii), d(iv)), N5 about 3 (d(i), d(iii)), black hole b(ii) 2.
Electron in a uniform electric field follows a line or parabola, never a circle (key A); it is electric-field motion, not magnetic.
1-mark MCQ (D): attractive force per unit length between parallel currents in the same direction; field of one wire (D.2) acting on the other (D.3).

a and b (4 marks) are reading the F-x graph gradient and intercept against the given equation; c and d (5) apply the gradient and intercept from the graph to get densities, so graph processing dominates. No uncertainty marks are asked, so F2 is not warranted.
Uncertainty in resistivity (c ii-iii, 4) and systematic thermometer error (d, 2) earn about 6 of 11; line of best fit with error bars and graph comparison are F4, design improvements (b) are F5.
E=V/d, F=qE, a=F/m in (a)(i),(ii) and (b)(i) earn 6 of 11 marks (E1); (a)(iii) projectile-style deflection is 3 marks (M1) and (b)(ii) B=E/v is 2 marks (E3).

Two-source interference c(iii), c(iv), d earns 7 marks, the biggest single subtopic; mechanics of the rope is about 10 marks but split across energy (4), Hooke/equilibrium/impulse (6). c(i) is SHM frequency (2).
